subject: computer-science
title: Big O: The Common Classes
welcome_lead: Five families of running time you must recognise on sight.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n^2).
final_note: Reading code in Big O becomes second nature with practice.

concepts.def: Asymptotic upper bound on a function's growth.
Constant time — independent of input size.
Logarithmic — doubling input adds one step.
Linear — time grows in proportion to input.

walkthroughs.body_html: O(1): array indexing, hash lookup (average). O(log n): binary search, balanced tree ops. Doubling n only adds one step in log time.
O(n): linear search, summing a list. O(n log n): merge sort, heapsort. The fastest possible comparison sorts hit this lower bound.
O(n^2): bubble sort, insertion sort, nested loops. Acceptable only for small inputs. Beyond this lie exponential and factorial running times — usually intractable.
